page: Microsoft Azure L64as_v4 is a storage and memory-focused server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 15,359 GB of local storage capacity and is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the L64as_v4 demonstrates strong multi-core performance, highlighted by a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21,342.0 and a strong stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 98,427.49. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth is strong at 4,861.79 GB/sec, large-block uncached read-only bandwidth falls into the average category at 150.96 GB/sec. The system also excels in database operations, achieving 89.18 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a strong Passmark database operations score. Large-scale data processing is supported by strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speeds of 366.38 GB/sec.

Given its massive 15 TB local storage capacity and 512 GB of RAM, the L64as_v4 offers high resource density for data-intensive workloads. It is highly suitable for large-scale databases, big data analytics, and high-throughput web serving. The presence of advanced CPU instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and cryptography extensions, enhances its efficiency for secure data processing and software compilation. The instance represents a qualitatively cost-effective option for workloads requiring substantial local storage and memory capacity without the overhead of dedicated GPU accelerators.
description: Microsoft Azure L64as_v4 is a high-capacity storage and memory-optimized server powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, it provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, paired with 512.0 GB of RAM and a substantial 15,359 GB of local storage. The instance delivers strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by its top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21,342.0 and strong multi-threaded decompression capabilities. Database operations are highly efficient, supported by strong Redis SET throughput and Passmark database scores. While memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, small-block cached reads are exceptionally fast. Lacking a GPU, this instance is qualitatively cost-effective for resource-dense, non-accelerated workloads. It is best suited for large-scale databases, data warehousing, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
